messages.subject: [R-SIG-Win] Rtools' additional package libsbml may mask MXE libsbml and lacks required extensions
messages.subject_clean: Rtools' additional package libsbml may mask MXE libsbml and lacks required extensions
messages.body_plain:
Dear Rtools maintainers,

I would like to report a potential issue with the libsbml library as 
currently distributed in Rtools (tested with Rtools45), and ask for 
guidance on how best to proceed.

I contributed the system library 'libsbml' to MXE. The MXE build of 
libsbml includes a number of extensions that are required by most common 
downstream use cases. The extensions are enables via optional parameters 
when building the library: 
https://github.com/mxe/mxe/blob/master/src/libsbml.mk

However, Rtools also distributes an additional libsbml package (outside 
of MXE), and this version appears to be built without several important 
extensions. My concern is that this Rtools-providedlibsbml may take 
precedence over the MXE-provided one (e.g., via PATH or pkg-config), 
effectively masking the new MXE version in upcoming Rtools revisions.

This creates a problem for potential R packages that depend on features 
provided by those extensions. I currently have an R package in 
preparation for CRAN submission that requires these capabilities, and I 
am concerned it may fail to build or function correctly on Windows due 
to this mismatch.

Currently, there seems to be no R packages on CRAN, that depends on 
libsbml. Even if there were, building such package should also succeed 
with the new MXE-provided libsbml.

A potential solution could be to avoid shipping libsbml in Rtools 
so?that the MXE-provided version is used consistently.

Best regards
Silvio
